title: Differentiate a learning activity
description: Keep a common learning goal while varying scaffolding, format and challenge.
accomplishes: Keep a common learning goal while varying scaffolding, format and challenge. Provide accessible instructions and optional extension tasks. Avoid fixed ability labels and explain how teacher observation guides adjustments rather than assuming learner needs.
prompt:
Act as an instructional designer.

Task: Differentiate a learning activity.

Input context:
- OBJECTIVE: [OBJECTIVE]
- LEARNER NEEDS: [LEARNER NEEDS]
- MATERIALS: [MATERIALS]
- TIME: [TIME]

Keep a common learning goal while varying scaffolding, format and challenge. Provide accessible instructions and optional extension tasks. Avoid fixed ability labels and explain how teacher observation guides adjustments rather than assuming learner needs.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Shared analysis activity
All learners identify an unsupported claim. One group receives highlighted passages, another a question guide and another an extension comparing sources. Allow a written or spoken explanation when appropriate. Adjust support from observed work. These options do not label learners permanently or establish which support any individual requires.
